paragraphs: Zedekiah's men came to Jeremiah hoping for a wonder, but they weren't asking for the LORD Himself. They wanted Nebuchadnezzar gone, and nothing in how they asked said anything about changing. The LORD answered with what He had been saying all along. A wonder can't fix a house that won't do what the LORD commanded (Jeremiah 21:2, 21:4-5).

Look at what the LORD asked of the house of David: "Administer justice every morning, and rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor." He also told the king to do no wrong or violence to the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow (Jeremiah 21:12; 22:3). Meanwhile, the ones on the rocky plateau said, "Who can come against us?" (Jeremiah 21:13). Friend, a great view is NOT the same as a safe place, and the only safe place is doing what the LORD says.

Then the LORD set two roads in front of them: "the way of life and the way of death." That's why the closing answer in the passage matters so much. People would say it was because "they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods" (Jeremiah 21:8; 22:9). So here's my big idea, baker: don't ask the LORD for wonders while you walk away from Him. Come back to Him, do what He says, and choose the road of life.
